rule: Intra-session carbohydrate 45-60 g/h (+ sodium) for sessions longer than the threshold
summary: Consensus is 30-60 g/h for exercise longer than ~1 h, and up to ~90 g/h (multiple transportable carbohydrates) beyond 2.5 h. A single carbohydrate source is oxidised at up to ~60 g/h. 45-60 g/h is the upper half of the standard range and is well supported for long runs and long Hyrox-style sessions. Meta-analyses confirm intra-session carbohydrate helps endurance performance more as sessions get longer, with no clear dose effect within the usual range. For runs or races longer than 2.5 h (marathon long runs, race day), compete should use 60-90 g/h glucose:fructose rather than this training default.

sources.note: Burke et al. 2011: 30-60 g/h for longer sessions; up to 90 g/h for events >2.5 h; ~1 h events: small amounts or mouth rinse
ISSN nutrient timing: ~30-60 g/h in a 6-8% solution for >60 min high-intensity bouts, especially >70 min
Jeukendrup 2014: single carbohydrate up to ~60 g/h for 2-3 h; ~90 g/h multiple transportable for ultra
136 studies: carbohydrate during endurance exercise improves performance, more with longer duration; dose not a moderator
